subject: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up (Acme Corp)

Alex / Sam —

Thanks again for the product demo earlier — really appreciate you walking through the primary QA use cases and the sample transcripts. Quick recap and agreed next steps: 

- Top takeaways: your eval targets are high-precision classification on short transcripts (avg 120 tokens) and stable behavior when callers reuse phrases.
- Recommended baseline models: small latency-sensitive variant (gpt-redwood-1.3-small-quant) for low-cost automated tagging, and gpt-redwood-2.1 for higher-quality reranking where precision > recall.
- I attached the prompt_set_v1.json we used in the call, plus the benchmark CSV showing our initial smoke tests against your sample data. Link to the full benchmark folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-ExampleBenchmark

Next steps (agreed):
1) You to share a 2k-row sample dataset for a deeper eval (Sam) — target by Wednesday 5/6.
2) We’ll run a 3-model sweep (small-quant, 1.3-standard, 2.1) with the attached prompt set and return a diff of precision/recall and latency by Friday 5/8.
3) If you see quality concerns, we’ll propose pinning a model version or rolling back a recent update — we’ll call out exact diffs in model outputs.

If this looks right I’ll schedule the eval run and loop in Rishi from infra for any model-version pinning requests.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up (Acme Corp)

Thanks Marissa — this matches our notes. I’ll get Sam to pull the 2k sample; should be over to you by Wednesday. Two quick questions before you run the sweep: 

1) Do you have a quick summary of what differences we should expect between the small-quant and 1.3-standard models on short transcripts? Mainly worried about named-entity precision.
2) We recently saw a drop in tagging precision after a recent internal update to our prompt templates. If your evals show regression, how fast can we pin to an older model version or request a rollback on Redwood’s side?

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Johnson

alex.johnson@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up (Acme Corp)

Alex — thanks, good questions. Short answers and plan: 

1) Quick model diff: small-quant (gpt-redwood-1.3-small-quant) is quantized for lower latency/cost; you should expect slightly lower recall on edge NER cases but comparable precision on high-confidence extractions. 1.3-standard has better raw quality and stability but ~2-3x cost. We’ll include per-intent precision/recall in the sweep.

2) Pinning / rollback: we can pin a customer route to a specific model version immediately from the control plane; rollback of a Redwood-hosted model to a previous variant is also doable but requires infra sign-off if it affects shared pools (we typically turn around urgent rollbacks within 24 hours). I’ve looped in Rishi to confirm process and ETA if we need an emergency rollback.

For transparency, I attached the prompt_set_v1.json and baseline benchmark CSV we’ll use for the sweep. If you’re able to send the sample dataset, we’ll start the runs and share a diff report showing any quality regressions (with example input/output pairs highlighted).

Action: Rishi — can you confirm the rollback/pinning SLAs and whether we can do a temporary route-pin that isolates Acme traffic to an earlier model build?

Thanks — Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 05 May 2026 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up (Acme Corp)

Looping in with the infra/ops perspective: 

- Pinning: we can pin a customer route to an exact model artifact (e.g., gpt-redwood-1.3-small-quant@v20260416) via the control plane; this is a config change and can be done in under 30 minutes during business hours. It ensures your production traffic hits the pinned artifact regardless of subsequent default model updates.

- Rollback: for hosted variants, we can revert a model rollout to the previous artifact. If the model update is only in a dedicated pool for Acme (reserved capacity), rollback is trivial and low risk. If the update was global to a shared pool, we schedule an emergency rollback; typical SLA for urgent rollbacks is ~24 hours but we’ll prioritize faster if the regression impacts production.

- Diff artifacts: when we run the sweep we’ll produce a granular diff report: per-example outputs, token-level edit distances, confidence/score distributions, and a short list of representative regression examples. That report will make it clear whether changes are model-degree (new weights) or prompt-template-related.

Proposed immediate plan:
1) Marissa / Acme: share the 2k sample and any changed prompt templates (Sam).
2) Redwood: run the 3-model sweep and deliver a diff report with a recommended action (pin to specific artifact OR rollback global update) — target Friday 5/8 for the initial report.
3) If regression is severe in production, Marissa/Acme can request an emergency route-pin and we’ll enact it within 30 minutes; for rollbacks we’ll target <24 hours.

I’ll also upload a short example diff (first 50 examples) to the shared Drive once the run completes.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
